# GC Missions conversion

Run from the GC Lobby checkout with Python 3.9+ and Git. The converter reads committed objects from the Missions repository. Fetch the two branches first. Supply commit hashes to reproduce a particular comparison.

```powershell
git -C ../gc-reforger-missions fetch origin master dev
python external/development/mission-conversion/convert.py --missions ../gc-reforger-missions --source origin/master --dev origin/dev --report "$env:TEMP/gc-missions-comparison.json" --stage "$env:TEMP/gc-missions-presets"
```

Omit `--stage` to compare without generating files. Use a new staging directory when inputs change. Repeating the same generation verifies existing output. Copy generated resource/metadata pairs into a clean Missions Dev checkout at the same relative paths. The tool checks existing tracked Dev presets for differing content. Review those differences before replacing any edited preset.


## Batch migration and file review

Use the batch workflow for the catalog. The same rules process every legacy launcher. They assemble complete drafts when all placements and behavior in a world match supported rules. Unrecognized constructs stay in the inventory with their file, line where available and conversion rule. The inventory groups blockers by the number of worlds affected, so a shared rule can unblock several missions on the next run.

Run the planner from GC Lobby with a clean Missions Dev checkout. Use a fresh output directory when the commits or conversion rules change.

    $repo = '../gc-reforger-missions'
    $tools = 'external/development/mission-conversion'
    $output = "$env:TEMP/gc-missions-plan"
    $base = 'C:/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/common/Arma Reforger/addons/data/resourceDatabase.rdb'
    $workshop = "$env:USERPROFILE/Documents/My Games/ArmaReforger/addons"
    python "$tools/plan_batch.py" --missions $repo --units ../gc-reforger-units --dependency ../gc-reforger-core --base-database $base --workshop-addons $workshop --output $output

Run the full file audit after a bundle of shared conversion changes. Install all drafts that clear source and Dev review, then choose the next bundle by how many worlds it can release. Start with complete drafts waiting on the same package and worlds waiting on the same conversion rules. The package table groups exact registrations from installed packages outside the Dev graph, so a terrain and all its navmeshes count as one lead. The asset table shows single-reference blockers and alternate registrations for closer review. Confirm prefab identity and behavior before accepting an alternate path. If a draft needs a custom port or unavailable asset, record the launcher, source location and missing behavior and keep processing the rest of the catalog.

The shared conversion queue estimates how many worlds each blocker bundle moves to the next file checks. It credits a world once and accounts for blockers removed by earlier rows. It uses the blockers the audit can currently see. Rebuild the queue after a bundle lands and keep mission-specific exceptions out of the bulk pass.

Use the file audit as the gate for routine batches. Once the bulk conversion is assembled, compile the shared Lobby scripts through Workbench MCP. Start with one Lobby-to-after-action smoke test covering role selection, briefing and map visibility, respawn and the match outcome. Use the same mission for any other checks it covers, then run up to four targeted representatives. The queue selects missions by behavior coverage. Continue with additional representatives when a release-critical behavior remains open or a failure calls for a retest. Reserve a legacy-versus-Dev playthrough for a runtime contract whose source files and existing evidence leave its behavior ambiguous.

Open `plan.md` for the number of committed launchers that cleared the file audit, the suggested batch of up to ten worlds and the reasons any generated drafts were held. The launcher audit below the coverage total includes the staged drafts. All launchers pointing at a drafted world travel together. `plan.json` gives source examples for each blocked conversion rule and ranks rules by the number of worlds where that rule is the only reported blocker, then by total worlds affected. Use the shared blocker combinations to tackle rules together. Some downstream checks run only when a draft is complete.

Use `sourceDependencyLeads` in `plan.json` to investigate resource registrations across held missions while shared conversion rules are in progress. Each lead lists the affected launchers, original references and installed registrations. A later rule may replace or remove a reference. Install decisions still use the completed draft and its declared dependencies.

Pass `--historical-workshop` with the archived addon directory when an authored launcher declares `m_aRequiredAddonVersions`. The audit checks each pinned launcher against its own reachable dependency graph and records the versions under `auditedAddonVersionsByLauncher`. Other launchers continue to use the standard graph. The installer and metadata capture preparation take one mounted graph per run. Use an isolated Workshop directory containing the declared versions for those steps. The capture report lists missing or incompatible version pins under `versionPinsOutsideScope`.

Use `outcomeFlagLeads` to find the exact event, serialized source fields and matching script literals for unresolved outcome flags. The Markdown plan counts worlds by the referenced component or trigger so related rules can be reviewed together. Check whether each source field reads or writes the flag before changing its conversion.

Stop each Workbench run once its assigned behaviors are verified. Record results against the tested revisions and list any checks still open. The full runtime queue is in `plan.json`. Pass that file with `--previous-plan` on the next audit to retain runtime checks on installed missions and inactive links confirmed by source inspection. When a check fails, fix the shared rule, rerun the file audit and repeat the affected runtime check.

`inventory.json` records conversion decisions and source locations. `review.md` and `review.json` compare every legacy launcher with the Dev snapshot overlaid with generated drafts. They report unchanged, changed, source-only and Dev-only files and locate declarations for modes, briefings, rosters, markers and boundaries, respawns, events, weather and vehicles. They also identify inconsistent launcher or resource references and name each file that uses an unresolved resource. Run `review.py` with repeatable `--mission` arguments and `--patch` for a focused diff. Omit `--draft-stage` to compare committed branches.

The migration generates Arma launcher and world resource registrations. The resource audit checks against the dependency graph declared by the Dev projects. The metadata table in `plan.md` separately reports GC headers, generated metadata snapshots, catalogue data, manual catalogue addon IDs and portable launch files committed in Dev. The standard GC launcher requires a generated snapshot or portable export. It resolves the snapshot's referenced addon names to GUIDs, includes the mission's owning addon, and adds any manual catalogue IDs. The portable exporter reports its own file count because it writes outside the checkout. Confirm script-selected content and use the supported exporter for the published build.

Probe unresolved prefab references from the plan together in one isolated Workbench world.

    python "$tools/resource_probe.py" --plan "$output/plan.json" --stage $resourceProbe

Open the generated `addon.gproj` and `worlds/Lookup.ent` through Workbench MCP. Opening the world logs each authored resource string and the resource that actually loaded. The probe mounts the base game by default. Repeat `--addon <GUID>` when the lookup needs specific installed providers. Read the results from that session's log.

    python "$tools/resource_probe.py" --plan "$output/plan.json" --console $probeConsole

An invalid result applies to the mounted graph. Confirm changed GUIDs or paths before adding them to conversion rules. The parser checks that the log contains one consistent result per planned prefab. The generated project reproduced all 23 results from the initial lookup in Workbench MCP session `logs_2026-11-21_15-27-18`.

Stage author catalogue fields from existing legacy GC metadata after running the file audit.

    python "$tools/author_catalogue.py" --missions $repo --audit "$output/plan.json" --stage $authorStage

This reads the legacy author fields defined in the published GC Core `GC_SCR_MissionHeader.c` and inserts the closest native equivalents for the original era, sides, force types, special assets and mission-group settings. The original author block stays byte for byte, including distinctions such as mortars versus other artillery that the current catalogue groups under one label. The report holds custom header types and unrecognized fields. Existing native catalogue entries take precedence.

The first pass mapped 36 author blocks, retaining the originals and all earlier generated snapshots. Junction Jab retained its era, Artillery tag, faction force descriptions and sides, and mission-group details through a native metadata refresh in Workbench session `logs_2026-11-21_12-15-42`. Its new snapshot and the 36 catalogue blocks are in Missions Dev commit `337e257d`.

Stage the header type for the native exporter with the same committed Dev revision used by the plan.

    python "$tools/launchers.py" --missions $repo --dev HEAD --prepare-metadata "$output/plan.json" --stage $metadataStage

Omit header paths for the entire file-cleared set. The preparation changes the root type on plain `SCR_MissionHeader` and stock Scenario Framework headers. The latter use `GC_ScenarioFrameworkMissionHeader`, which inherits their native task, despawn and faction overrides. Existing GC headers can go directly to metadata collection. Other custom header types are reported for review. The native exporter fills the generated snapshot using the mission subscene, and the direct launcher exports the portable file from that saved header.

Kassel Crashers Modern Redux retained its Scenario Framework header family and original author block in Missions Dev commit `ee9cee2d`. Workbench session `logs_2026-11-21_12-28-55` saved a native snapshot of 1,298 entities and round-tripped the translated catalogue, including its `KasselCrashers` group and 0.75 similarity. The rebuilt portable launcher exported the original mission and world identities. Across the rest of the draft set, the new header support changed only the root type in Al Hadra Rumble's existing draft.

Use the full Missions Dev project for native metadata collection when its dependencies compile. To collect limited snapshots while full compilation is blocked, stage the Base and Lobby cohort from the audited revisions.

    python "$tools/prepare_metadata_capture.py" --missions $repo --lobby $lobbyRepo --audit "$output/plan.json" --base-database $baseDatabase --stage $capture

The command copies the committed mission resources to a new directory outside both checkouts and prints a JSON report mapping eligible headers to worlds. It records references outside the capture scope per excluded header. Open the staged `addon.gproj` and the eligible worlds through Workbench MCP. Use **GC → Create Mission Data → Refresh metadata only** on each world. The fixture keeps the Missions Dev identity and limits its dependency list to Base and Lobby. Metadata from this fixture describes the resources observed in that scope. Full-project addon overrides, script-selected content and launch behavior still require verification.

For a known broken dependency, use the retained project graph to capture a wider cohort.

    python "$tools/prepare_metadata_capture.py" --missions $repo --lobby $lobbyRepo --audit "$output/plan.json" --base-database $baseDatabase --workshop $workshop --dependency-checkout $coreRepo --dependency-checkout $unitsRepo --exclude-addon 5994614FB5AD35C2 --stage $capture

The stage removes the excluded addon and any root dependency that requires it. It rejects worlds with saved resources unavailable in the retained graph or with a resource GUID supplied by an excluded addon. The exclusion only applies to the isolated project. The native scanner still needs to succeed for each eligible world, and indirect resource resolution is limited to the mounted graph. The regular capture holds explicit faction catalogue overrides under `authoredCataloguesForReview`. Add `--only-authored-catalogues` to stage just those worlds and report the exact asset registrations and their addon IDs.

Merge a native metadata capture from an isolated copy of the same Dev files with the same command and `--native-exports $capture`. Supply header paths to select a subset. The merger verifies the captured world, local layers, referenced resources and registration files against Dev. It copies only the generated snapshot so a Workbench re-save cannot remove legacy catalogue fields from the Dev header. After committing the merged header and rerunning the audit, export the file-cleared headers that have snapshots through the standard launcher.

Use the batch installer to merge and apply captures without copying individual headers. The command previews changes by default. Add `--apply` to write the audited batch to a clean Missions checkout, then commit it and rerun the audit.

    python "$tools/install_metadata.py" --missions $repo --audit "$output/plan.json" --capture $capture $headers

The installer applied the 18 snapshots in Missions Dev commit `e9f3e1f3`. The dry run left the checkout clean. A modified captured layer failed verification, and a simulated later write failure restored the earlier writes.

Race Day Kunar's first launcher export found its original world path in the renamed world's registration file. Missions Dev commit `7147e3a7` corrected the registered path and kept the world GUID. The audit and capture installer now check both the path and the unique GUID registration.

Missions Dev commit `6bdbb026` adds 19 snapshots. Workbench crashed while opening Falcons Flight in session `logs_2026-11-21_13-01-50` and Kasselberg Clamber in `logs_2026-11-21_13-06-11`. Both captured successfully after starting a fresh editor session. The installer verified all 19 captured worlds against the same Dev revision before applying them.

    & "$tools/export_metadata.ps1" -Missions $repo -Plan "$output/plan.json" -Output $portableStage

For authored catalogue captures, pass the catalogue staging report as `-CatalogueReport`. The exporter compares the authored source blobs against the committed mission and verifies that each non-stock provider appears in the portable addon's required list before publishing the file.

Huey Hill's schema 2 snapshot is in Missions Dev commit `ff74a01f`. The isolated export read 58 entities from the exact Dev mission files. Direct resource ownership checks found all saved references in Missions Dev, Lobby Dev or the base game. The native snapshot reports partial coverage and 3,260 unexpanded resources. The standard launcher exported the merged header using its original scenario and world IDs. The full Missions Dev project mounted its declared dependencies, but its installed RHIB package `5994614FB5AD35C2` prevented Game module compilation with unknown `VehicleDust` references in `SPC_BoatSplash.c`. See Workbench session `logs_2026-11-21_11-22-28`, lines 28659–28688. Launch verification with the full dependency graph remains open.

Coastal Clearance and Last Bastion have schema 2 snapshots in Missions Dev commit `03c4d0ff`. Workbench read 163 entities from each isolated world. The merger verified each captured mission's files against Dev and installed only the generated snapshot. Both exports record partial resource coverage. At that revision, the other 169 file-cleared GC headers without snapshots had saved references beyond the Base and Lobby capture scope.

The retained graph without RHIB compiles in Workbench session `logs_2026-11-21_11-45-22`. Of the 169 headers outside the original capture scope, 161 passed the saved-reference check against that graph. The original one-million-container scan limit stopped the first 10 attempts. An expanded scan produced nearly five-megabyte headers for Hnevice and Montignac Meat Grind. Hnevice retained 9,496 rows, including 5,337 first reached through faction entity catalogues.

Workbench session `logs_2026-11-21_11-57-03` verified the scan with inherited faction catalogue alternatives omitted. Hnevice dropped from 4,966,794 to 743,115 bytes and from 116 to 66 observed addon names. Montignac Meat Grind dropped from 5,055,251 to 746,773 bytes and from 116 to 62 names. Generated slots, factions and asset totals matched the original captures, and the merger confirmed that the saved mission files matched Dev. Nine snapshots are in Missions Dev commit `74493ef4`.

A temporary test added a unique prefab to an explicit faction catalogue in OSI The Airfield Incident. Its passive metadata scan did not identify that reference, so catalogue-only coverage remains unverified. The capture gate holds that mission, The Bear Went Over the Mountain and Top Malo House for separate review of their authored catalogue fields. That audit reported 149 remaining captures in the retained graph and eight headers with saved references outside it. The captures describe the retained graph and full-project launch verification remains open.

Missions Dev commit `864db503` adds the three catalogue review snapshots and 17 further snapshots. The Bear Went Over the Mountain has no direct asset references in its authored catalogue. OSI The Airfield Incident has eight direct references. Its native snapshot resolves all five with non-stock providers, and its launch export includes all four required non-stock addon IDs. Top Malo House captured 375 entities in Workbench session `logs_2026-11-21_12-46-40`. All 13 direct catalogue assets resolve to Units Dev and the launch export includes that addon. The 13 catalogue entries remain absent from the native snapshot's individual resource rows. The catalogue report records the exact registrations and source blob IDs used for these checks.

The staging preflight follows the base game's declared Engine Core dependency, which registers Breach and Clear's stock particle editor resource. It also accepts the exact path-loaded Longmoor parent for Bug Out, Longmoor Lashings and both Foreign Exchange Students missions, using the same verified Workshop archive and sole-reference check as the file audit. These five worlds passed staging. The next twelve snapshots are in Missions Dev commit `18f13864` and came from the RHIB-excluded graph.

The five recovered worlds all produced native snapshots in Workbench session `logs_2026-11-21_12-15-42`. The migration checked the captured mission files against Dev and installed only the snapshots. The same batch captured ten additional missions in Missions Dev commit `7ddd3809`.

The batch in `ee9cee2d` also includes Clearing Out Gorshkovo and 15 other HitTheMan missions. Gorshkovo crashed Workbench after loading in session `logs_2026-11-21_12-25-55`. A fresh, single-mission fixture with the same saved files and retained dependency graph captured 416 entities in session `logs_2026-11-21_12-35-21`. The merge passed the unchanged-file check. The initial crash's cause remains unverified.

Taking Trenches, North Coast Raid and Privateering directly reference RHIB. Workbench session `logs_2026-11-21_12-11-06` mounted the full, unmodified Dev manifest in a separate fixture with a local, data-only `VehicleDust` class for the installed RHIB 1.0.20 script. Game scripts compiled and the three metadata captures loaded 134, 148 and 32 entities, respectively. Each snapshot recorded RHIB GUID `5994614FB5AD35C2`. The merger verified the original mission files and committed the generated snapshots in `3a752f65`. The fixture's compatibility class was excluded from the commit. The unmodified installation still needs a compatible RHIB update to compile for representative playtesting.

Missions Dev commit `7be0f322` adds 19 snapshots from the retained graph. Workbench crashed loading a subsequent world in session `logs_2026-11-21_13-18-28`. A fresh process in session `logs_2026-11-21_13-23-57` captured the five outstanding worlds from the same fixture. All 19 passed the unchanged-file check. The full file audit cleared 173 launchers, including 136 with snapshots and 37 with catalogue data. All 136 portable exports passed checks for the committed header hash, world path and required addon GUID format. That leaves 37 file-cleared launchers awaiting capture.

Missions Dev commit `082f9dd1` adds the next 19 snapshots from the retained graph. The same file and export checks passed for 155 launchers. The preflight staged all 18 remaining file-cleared launchers for Workbench capture.

Missions Dev commit `3dfacb6e` adds those 18 snapshots from Workbench session `logs_2026-11-21_13-38-10`. San Serriffe Busters adds one more converted launcher and snapshot in `603c2440` and `c81f3b6e`. Its native snapshot captured 97 entities and 72 roles in session `logs_2026-11-21_13-46-23`. All 174 file-cleared launchers now have a generated snapshot and passed the portable launch metadata export checks.

After reviewing the file-cleared drafts, give the installer its plan with `--all-ready` to install them in one pass. The installer checks that the plan came from the exact inventory and validates file hashes, paths, collisions and resources before writing. Omit `--all-ready` to install only the suggested batch. Review the committed files and push grouped deliveries of roughly ten launchers. The number of launchers in a push is independent of the size of the local install.

    python "$tools/install_batch.py" --missions $repo --inventory "$output/inventory.json" --stage "$output/drafts" --plan "$output/plan.json" --all-ready --dependency . --dependency ../gc-reforger-units --dependency ../gc-reforger-core --base-database $base --workshop-addons $workshop

The installer leaves Git commits and pushes to the delivery batch. It refuses to overwrite differing files unless the planner records them as reviewed and the installer is given `--replace-reviewed`. The review resolves file identities and records supported conversions. Runtime checks cover new framework features, historical terrain revisions and inherited behavior that the file rules cannot account for. Apply Workbench evidence for a shared feature to the relevant conversion rule across missions.

The AI reinforcement rule uses the existing `GC_AIGroupSpawn` action. It preserves the instruction delay, named placement, optional entity name and order of appended waypoints. The planner verifies the stock group, its group parents and its character roster against the installed registrations and checks for overrides in the Missions and Units snapshots. A completed world draft must also have one placed anchor and one placed AI waypoint for each referenced name. Custom group prefabs and stock groups with overridden roster members stay in the file review until their ancestry and loadouts are verified. The legacy behavior was reviewed in `TILW_Instructions.c` and `TILW_CrewConfig.c` from the published TilW Mission Framework package through the Reforger MCP archive tools.

The event converter uses the placed-vehicle crew rule for structured event spawns. It preserves ordered stations, named waypoints, delays and the legacy gunner options. Custom or unavailable vehicle and character references still require review. The event notification rule preserves headings when the legacy hint supplied only a title. It still reports instructions with neither a heading nor a body. The published TilW hint handler passes both fields independently to the base-game hint manager. Workbench MCP compiled the native title-only notification change with zero errors in session `logs_2026-11-20_20-05-55`. Client display and audience delivery are part of the representative runtime check.

The batch converter retains rotated and uniformly scaled map shapes and validates the polygon projected onto the world XZ plane. An auxiliary outline becomes a separate native map shape with the original colour, audience and line width in metres. Its width is evaluated as the larger of one pixel and line width times zoom. The legacy TilW AO, map shape and cover components all use `CoordToParent`. The projection follows the base-game `AnglesToMatrix` example. These rules apply to new drafts. Earlier converted cover layers with screen-width outlines and client rendering still need review.

The converter handles top-level, unrotated, unit-scale shapes with an explicitly enabled cover component and disabled AO. It keeps the authored name and origin and emits the native map-only mask. The published `TILW_CoverMapComponent.c` (lines 19–86) computes the cover independently of AO enforcement. The published AO prefab also disables its auxiliary map shape by default, including when an instance supplies style overrides without enabling it. The audit verified the authored aspect ratio and black mask bounds in Serriff Busters, Supply Secure at Montignac and Commandos Reforged. Supply Secure at Montignac and Commandos Reforged still have other open blockers. All 254 existing draft files remained byte-identical. Compare client framing when these missions clear their other checks.

The San Serriffe Busters mode now retains its empty native `SCR_CampaignBuildingManagerComponent` placement, the authored 06:15 rainy start and the Donovian callsign overrides. The published mode ancestry contains no override of that placement ID. The native manager reads its default values when the placement supplies none. The source-to-Dev review matched every ordered prefab GUID and group location across the archived and converted rosters, with 28 San Serriffe and 44 Donovian roles. Workbench reported the same faction totals. The header keeps its 71-player listing. All 254 earlier draft files were byte-identical. Client map framing, callsigns, weather at Match start and building interactions remain in runtime review.

PowerPlay now retains its zero-grace Separatist boundary, the native empty group-flag override and both stock power-pole placements. The published TilW AO starts its timer on exit and forces death on the next fixed-frame update when the authored timer is zero. The native soft AO uses zero grace on the first server evaluation after an enrolled player exits. The file check matched the authored polygon and faction and verified both pole transforms and the serialized group-flag override. Workbench reloaded the script change with zero errors in session `logs_2026-11-21_14-10-12`, lines 27707–27776. A live boundary crossing remains unverified.

Workbench loaded the published PowerPlay world in `logs_2026-11-21_14-19-29`. It reported all five `m_vRespawnPosition` fields as unknown keywords on the legacy AI groups. The converter skips this obsolete field while preserving native faction respawn tickets and group transforms. The same session rejected `PK_Ruha_Power_Plant.nmn` as obsolete during soldier navigation initialization. The compiled mesh and all 1,163 original tiles match the published archive byte for byte. The audit counts those tiles in the mission's resource closure and holds the obsolete compiled mesh for regeneration and a pathfinding comparison. The fire prefab, group color teams and repeated `ReleaseOpfor` producer also remain open. All 254 prior draft files remained byte-identical.

PowerPlay's six `ReleaseOpfor` triggers can each overwrite the shared flag. The published `TILW_BaseTriggerEntity.c` writes on first discovery and when an area's result changes, including changes back to false. Any native conversion must retain those writes and their ordering. Nagalam Traffic Jam also has five pairs of co-located trigger volumes with different owner factions. Those pairs retain separate conditions and remain in review.

Placed spawners now retain positive uniform scale on the native spawn anchor. The published `TILW_PrefabSpawnerEntity.c` and native spawn action both pass the placement's world transform to the engine. Nagalam Traffic Jam's blocked-road spawn retains the `0.977` scale, coordinates, three authored angles and `QRF_Arrived` area condition. Its Afghan granite cliff matches the prefab body in Arma Terrain Core 1.1.7. The converter verifies the current provider archive and exact GUID and path, and the normal file review checks the dependency graph. Live placement remains in representative review.

The mode rule preserves verified legacy faction, radio, chat, preview and editor child settings using the corresponding native Lobby entities. The published legacy Lobby placement and base-game preview prefab provide the reference defaults. Framework transforms can be omitted when every event was converted because the legacy framework does not use its own transform. `m_safeStartTime` was inactive in the published GC Core character controller. Its only call to `HandleSafestart` is commented out, and the legacy mission scripts contain no callers. The mode keeps the independent staging countdown. Hall Boss and Hall Boss Mines retain 75 advertised players and all 47 authored slots each. Capacity approvals check the original header and both roster layer hashes.

The ten Roulette worlds share the authored `GC_R_Manager` and map-specific scenario choices. Their briefing and mode blockers cover a shared runtime migration. The legacy manager rerolls seeded scenarios, regenerates groups, spawns descriptions and map overlays, and builds capture, casualty and time-limit outcomes through the old framework. Keep its map-specific configuration and authored command descriptions with the runtime port. Verify that the shared generator publishes the roster before role selection, replaces only its own state on reroll, and resolves outcomes in Match. The old sphere queries and global player controller hook require supported replacements.

Prepare the shared inputs for all ten worlds in a single run.

    python "$tools/roulette.py" --missions $repo --source $legacyRevision --output $rouletteStage

The external stage contains native presets for the static commands page and `roulette.json` with the three ordered scenario definitions, their prefab references, the per-world overrides and the original source blob IDs. The stage retains Arland's fieldless scenario entry, Kunar's 1,400-metre minimum and its separate command text, and Zarichne's 1,200-metre minimum. Two runs reproduced all 11 files byte for byte. The source comparison matched all 10 command descriptions, the full authored fields of all three scenarios and 68 distinct resource references. Use those references in the dependency audit for the dynamically generated content. The stage stays external until the native generator, commands, objectives and briefing visibility can be verified together.

Use the declared Dev dependency graph to check the generated prefabs and prepare the mission-owned inventory crate.

    python "$tools/roulette.py" --missions $repo --source $legacyRevision --output $rouletteStage --base-database $baseDatabase --workshop-addons $workshop --units $unitsRepo --units-source $legacyUnitsRevision --dependency $coreRepo --dependency $lobbyRepo

The graph check retains the original GUIDs and replaces only three Canadian group paths and the capitalization of the drone inventory prefab. Units Dev commit `392f8c07` corrects the three group registrations to the physical paths already used by the published Units registry. The three groups retain all original ordered slots and inherited role prefabs. The description field is the normal Lobby metadata migration. The folded paper map overlay moved from Core to Units with identical resource and metadata blobs. The crate keeps its registration, original controller, goggles and inventory slots. Two graph-checked stages produced 13 byte-identical files and verified all 72 distinct direct references across the authored scenarios and crate. The runtime port still needs to capture and verify per-mission launch metadata for the generated content.

The graph-checked stage also writes one registered native scenario catalogue and a registered map configuration for each world. The map configurations refer to the same catalogue and keep the ordered overrides separately. Two runs reproduced all 35 outputs and the file comparison matched each native scenario body to its audited fields and all ten map configurations to their source overrides.

Missions Dev commit `ff2cdca6` adds the native config types and roster allocator. It counts the existing group prefab slots, keeps company, platoon and squad presentation order, and clears the pending plan if a selected group cannot be loaded. The isolated dedicated-server check in `logs_2026-11-21_17-13-19` loaded all three scenarios with 6, 5 and 6 teams, three briefings each, and Kunar's 1,400-metre minimum. With a five-slot stock group it verified selection with and without a headquarters and rollback on an invalid group. Workbench compiled the script, then crashed while opening its previously selected world. The fixture verified serialization and roster planning. Scenario placement, actual lobby registration, changing a live roster, and match outcomes remain open.

Missions Dev commit `154ecccd` adds seeded scenario and team selection and applies the legacy team-strength ratio to the selected groups. The seed advances through the same scenario and team draws when an administrator supplies explicit indices. The dedicated check in `logs_2026-11-21_17-17-01` compared two rolls for each of 50 seeds, checked faction blacklists and water capability on 100 automatic pairings, verified forced team order and rejected an out-of-range index. For a target of 18 with the five-slot fixture groups it selected 10 defending and 20 attacking slots, using the selected defender count for the attacker target. Native configs loaded Arland's 2,000-metre default and the 1,400- and 1,200-metre overrides in Kunar and Zarichne.

Missions Dev commit `374c63ce` adds the shared terrain search. It offers bounded objective and bearing attempts, uses native box queries filtered by radial bounds, and keeps the authored building density, prefab exclusions, water run, hexagonal clearance and slope checks. Two initial attempts on unchanged terrain returned candidates in different broadphase order. The port sorts by coordinates and prefab name before the seeded draw. Dedicated sessions `logs_2026-11-21_17-21-55` and `logs_2026-11-21_17-22-19` each reproduced the same Arland objective and two deployment locations for seed 15415, with zero coordinate difference across repeated queries. The attacker was 2,005.63 metres from the objective and the defender 79.37 metres away. The sorted search makes the new rollout repeatable. Exact objective coordinates for a legacy seed, other terrain packages, and live roster placement still need comparison.

The converter now checks the 53 selected group prefabs against Units Dev and generates seven local wrappers that add only native playability. Both staging runs produced 49 byte-identical files. Missions Dev commit `57b747ac` places generated groups and vehicles through the native spawn path, with Lobby handling registration and slot creation. Replacement is limited to setup and groups with no claims or prepared player bodies. The previous generated entities stay alive until the replacement roster is valid. Native callsign assignment requests the legacy group indices after retiring the old roster and retains the native fallback when an index is unavailable.

The dedicated check in `logs_2026-11-21_17-34-45` ran against the Lobby mode and a registered five-slot group prefab. It verified two new groups with valid replication IDs and five slots each, failure after one pending group spawns, preservation of the old slot IDs on failure, removal of those slots on success, and retention of the unrelated authored group. The original test prefab had no resource database entry and produced no replication IDs even though it could be spawned locally. The final test used a registered prefab and the production check rejects unreplicated groups in network play. Remote slot refresh, full roster callsign parity, the automatic generation entry point, and match rules remain open.

Missions Dev commit `2b5c7838` adds the startup component. The graph-checked stage wires each mode preset to its map config. Both runs reproduced 49 files byte for byte. The component loads the catalogue on the server, limits terrain attempts per callback, and publishes the roster before permitting Lobby slotting or briefing. A configured seed gets one attempt. Automatic startup tries up to eight seeds and leaves the setup gate closed if none succeeds. The phase gate belongs to the opted-in mode component, and ordinary Lobby worlds retain their existing phase checks.

The dedicated fixture in `logs_2026-11-21_17-40-06` started from the generated Arland settings and a small fixture catalogue with registered group prefabs. The gate started closed, and seed 15415 published two replicated five-slot groups while Lobby stayed in PREGAME. The authority also applied the generated date of 1988-06-23 and Overcast weather. The check exercised server startup, role readiness and environment setup. Admin commands, the generated objective and briefing overlays, outcome rules and a full authored roster remain open.

Missions Dev commit `dd161c4f` ports the four Roulette outcome events to the native Lobby engine. The named capture area uses the selected building's largest horizontal dimension times 1.25, with a 15-metre minimum. It retains the all-attacker local share, five-minute elapsed hold, six notices, discovery and single interruption deduction from the published Roulette capture prefab and TilW base/faction trigger scripts. The two casualty routes use the existing peak-player observer, give notice when 95 percent loss is reached and finish ten seconds later. The time limit announces ten seconds early and awards the defending faction the win. The native result completes on the next countdown update for this opted-in action. The default two-minute ending remains for ordinary End Mission actions.

The dedicated fixture with a 12-second limit reached the expected US defending victory after 12.5 seconds in `logs_2026-11-21_17-47-08`. With a longer limit, the empty-team casualty fixture reached the expected USSR attacking victory after 15.55 seconds in `logs_2026-11-21_17-49-00`. The latter also drove the native capture state with elapsed-time inputs and confirmed the single interruption deduction and first-change latch. These fixtures exercise native match completion and capture state. Contested live player capture, casualty counts with occupied factions and notice delivery to remote players remain verification items. Both staging runs reproduced all 49 files, with the generated-rule setup and casualty observer attached to every mode preset.

Missions Dev commit `ea7c6f5d` publishes the three scenario briefings through Lobby's replicated catalogue. It substitutes the generated environment, team names, order of battle and counts of the vehicles actually spawned. General pages are available to all viewers and the two team pages are restricted to their respective factions. The converter keeps the static Commands page at index 31 so the generated pages can use their authored order. The objective remains a red 100-metre circle and the two spawn markers use 40-pixel faction flags.

The ten stages also have a separate authority-owned AO layer. One four-point polygon drives both enforcement and the inverted map fill. The published `RouletteAO.et`, TilW AO/shape scripts, and PS Core marker prefab provide the original geometry, 20-second soft boundary, black 75-percent exterior mask, and three-pixel black outline. A nested mode child was not registered as a named shape in the dedicated fixture. The separate layer resolved the name and its placeholder stays disabled until the generated geometry is applied. The dedicated test in `logs_2026-11-21_18-00-22` verified the three briefing audiences for assigned and unassigned viewers, two vehicle lists, all three markers, and matching four-point map and enforcement geometry. Both stages reproduced all 59 files. Client rendering and actual out-of-bounds expiry remain representative runtime checks.

Missions Dev commit `ecfa02b8` ports `/seed`, `/scenario`, `/teams`, `/players`, and `/reroll` through the owning GC Lobby controller. Read-only lists and the published seed are available to connected players. Setup mutations require active admin login, and queued rerolls recheck both login and account identity before each generation step. The dedicated fixture in `logs_2026-11-21_18-04-24` rejected two unresolved requester IDs, recorded both in the admin audit log, and kept the published roster unchanged. Connected logged-out rejection, authenticated command execution and remote chat replies still need a representative client check.

To install the complete file-reviewed Roulette batch, add `--assemble` to the graph-checked stage command and use `roulette.json` as the standard installer's inventory.

    python "$tools/install_batch.py" --missions $repo --inventory "$rouletteStage/roulette.json" --stage $rouletteStage --base-database $baseDatabase --workshop-addons $workshop --dependency $unitsRepo --dependency $coreRepo --dependency $lobbyRepo --dry-run

The stage preserved the ten registered header and terrain identities, shared File formation, and the four original faction relationship entries on the nine inherited modes. Kunar uses its original local mode configuration without those inherited overrides. Bystrany retains its custom map placement and uses the registered current topology. Everon's original demo event checks the unpublished `test` flag and was replaced with the same generated events as in the other Roulette worlds. Two assembly runs reproduced all 121 outputs. All ten passed the file comparison and the installer verified 127 distinct resource references. The 120 installed files match Missions Dev commit `027be177` byte for byte. The retained dependency graph resolves 117 launch asset references across the three scenario catalogues and ten worlds. The assembler records 10 or 11 explicit required addon IDs per header so the launch manifests include alternate rolls. Workbench captured all ten native snapshots, and the portable exports match the committed header hashes and world references and include all audited providers. The native scan covers authored entities and reports partial coverage for generated runtime content.

Dedicated startup on the authored Arland and Kunar worlds generated 110 and 120 roles, respectively. Kunar also confirmed the revised automatic seed initialization. Both authored startup runs rolled Cold War. The fixture exercised all three scenarios, and connected-player admin login and remote command replies remain unverified.

The mission-owned APC crew characters in Heaven and Hell and Hot Boxes, plus the gunner in Abad Day in Kunar US TVT, share the unresolved DCU rifleman parent `EA6EF9C87D023B9B`. The installed Units archive registers the similarly named playable wrapper as `62DF528A4FF16F25`. Units commit `ffb3a751` confirms that wrapper already inherited the missing parent. Redirecting the reference to the wrapper would leave the underlying appearance and equipment unresolved. The exact parent or a verified equivalent remains necessary to clear these roles.

The batch audit now links unresolved parent references to the exact mission-owned roster slots they block. It reports the affected worlds and identifies when one parent accounts for every reported blocker in a world. The DCU rifleman is the only reported blocker for Heaven and Hell and one of several for the other two missions. Workbench session `logs_2026-11-21_14-36-12` also returned an invalid resource for the DCU parent.

The same Workbench session resolved the stale Bootnecks and BTRs Runner parent to the current `A491F9108F01E180` Units rifleman and rejected the missing deputy platoon leader parent. The converter keeps the Runner's resolved loadout and uses the exact archived deputy parent already recovered in Units Dev. The original groups expressly force both characters playable. The file check preserved their authored equipment references and the Runner label. Bootnecks and BTRs still requires staging protection. All 254 existing draft files stayed byte-identical.

Five HotMic missions define numbered framework callbacks directly in their legacy `default.layer`. The published TilW framework dispatches these callbacks through `RequestRunScript` and applies its per-number rerun setting. Their authored effects require native replacements before the event converter can clear them.

| Mission | Authored callback behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Delaying Action Ruha Platoon | Tracks spawned phase units by instance, renames them uniquely and deletes the tracked set on cleanup. |
| Operation Concrete Crushers | Counts collected intel, maps selected town flags to spawn flags and faction hints, and removes inactive intel entities and markers. |
| Stop the FOOD Market at Kunar | Resolves the named supply depot and advances on thresholds of 500 and 1,000 supplies. |
| Supply Secure at Montignac | Compares the named depots' aggregated supplies. A tie selects Red. Missing entities or resource components set the authored error flag. |
| Vehicle Interdiction COOP Kunar | Fills the selected cargo van with 250 supplies and checks the receiving depot for exactly 250, with authored setup failure handling. |

Owl’s Prey, The Adjacent Wave and Zarichne Front place AI with `EnableAI 1` and an explicit soldier behavior override. The published TilW Mission Framework archive contains `AI/BehaviorTrees/Chimera/Soldier/TILW_StaticAI.bt`. Its parallel branches observe for targets and process attack, idling and danger. Preserve the placed sentry behavior with a GC-owned or native equivalent before allowing the converter to rewrite those characters. A stock defend waypoint alone does not establish parity for individually placed characters.

The pinned source contains 46 references across Owl’s Prey (7), The Adjacent Wave (24), Zarichne Front (14) and Bebble Island Raid (1). An external Arland fixture compared a stock rifleman, the native idle-speed setting, the native character movement-control lock, and the published TilW tree. All four fired at the same target placement. The stock and idle-speed variants moved 3.46 and 4.67 metres from their sampled start positions. The lock and the legacy tree each stayed at zero displacement for all 30 samples. See `logs_2026-11-21_16-22-29`, `logs_2026-11-21_16-23-08`, `logs_2026-11-21_16-23-45` and `logs_2026-11-21_16-25-05` in the external sentry profiles. The movement-control lock is the verified candidate for authored sentries. Validate its lifetime and release on player possession, and compare danger response and target reacquisition before accepting the conversion.

The opt-in `GC_StaticSentryComponent` applies the native movement lock only to AI-controlled characters in an active GC Lobby world. The external dedicated run in `logs_2026-11-21_16-29-22` exercised the production component. The character fired with zero sampled displacement, released the lock when AI was deactivated and reacquired it on reactivation. In `logs_2026-11-21_16-34-35`, the same authored component was present under the stock game mode and all three checks found movement unlocked. Live player possession, danger response and target reacquisition remain representative checks.

Missions Dev commit `97247030` preserves all 24 sentries in The Adjacent Wave and 14 in Zarichne Front under the original character IDs and transforms. RHS Status Quo registers the original Adjacent Wave sergeant prefab. Zarichne retains all 67 ordered roster entries under the authored 65-player listing and adds 10 briefing pages to the existing settings preset. Its existing native events and settings match the earlier preset. The conversion audit reproduced 254 prior draft files byte for byte. Owl’s Prey and Bebble Island Raid retain other blockers in the audit.

Workbench session `logs_2026-11-21_16-33-57` captured 174 entities in The Adjacent Wave and 401 in Zarichne Front. Missions Dev commit `37b6a6a1` stores both snapshots. The standard launcher exports verified the original scenario and world IDs, the committed header hashes and the required lists of 52 and 69 addon IDs, respectively.

Owl's Prey retains all seven authored sentries. Snake Island 1.0.18 registers the original terrain, AI world, helicopter and body material. Missions Dev commit `bd7e026c` declares that dependency and `e4b0b490` installs the world and launcher. The ordered comparison matched 37 original roles under the authored 38-player listing. Workbench loaded the Snake Island parent and scanned 52 entities in `logs_2026-11-21_16-40-06`. Commit `9ef3e3e6` stores the native snapshot, and the standard portable launch export includes Snake Island among 51 required addons. The file audit reproduced 270 prior staged files byte for byte. Legacy flight equipment, startup selection and compound outcome timing stay in the representative runtime queue. [Snake Island release history](https://reforger.armaplatform.com/workshop/5D2C09EC3A5DF8AD-SnakeIsland-Ukraine/changelog)

Route Rowan cleared the file audit in Missions Dev commit `3d6505c4`. The converter uses the original polygon rings for the three capture checks and preserves the faction overlays and named child anchors. Archive inspection confirmed that the appended US Medic wrapper only adds playability to the stock medic. The native playable group retains that final slot for a total of 37. The current WCS catalogue registers the Marine Cobra at its new path under the original GUID. The batch updates the AO exemption to the same path and preserves both disabled weapon stations using their current WCS types and original container IDs. The WCS catalogue and Cobra base prefab were inspected through Reforger MCP catalogue revision `fd450f54a66d4d0d939ed2c66547b701`. Live capture, teleports, respawn ticket changes and Cobra behavior remain in the representative test queue.

Workbench MCP refreshed Route Rowan's header from 1,470 entities in `logs_2026-11-21_14-53-41`. The snapshot identifies the registered Cobra plus its addon and the WCS armaments dependency. Missions Dev commit `30134e53` adds that snapshot. Capture used the retained addon graph with RHIB omitted. The world loaded with diagnostics for inherited dependency resources, including unresolved faction-catalogue entries. The file audit and capture do not verify full-graph play.

Two Bloody Miles uses the same polygon rule for its visible end-state objective and four intentionally hidden capture areas. Its two delayed waves test the live inverse of their immediate area checks and schedule six groups each at 900 and 1,800 seconds respectively. The placed spawner rule uses one shared first-positive event per verified capture flag. It keeps each spawner's authored delays, seats and waypoints. Losing the area later leaves already scheduled spawns active during Match. The rule checks for one producer and accounts for the serialized flag readers. The source behavior comes from TilW's `TILW_PrefabSpawnerEntity.c` and `TILW_Instructions.c`.

A focused file check rendered the two authored BRDM spawners with one shared 1% capture check, their original crew definitions and the `snd4` waypoint. The installed Tactical Flava registrations also cleared the tan AGS and KORD TIGRs and the single-seat AGS tripod. The audit verified that `qrf13`, `qrf14` and `qrf15` are unused random flags. The complete 277-launcher comparison reproduced all 254 existing drafts byte for byte. Live wave and reinforcement timing remains open.

Two Bloody Miles retains its 28 authored AO vertices and adds four points placed 5 mm along the two crossing edges. The converter only enables this correction for the reviewed source layer blob. The native polygon validator accepts the result with the original 20-second grace and M777 exemption. Across 126,481 positions, full-precision membership changes were confined to within 7 mm of the crossing. At engine coordinate precision, the sampled changes farther away were within 0.31 mm of an original edge. Live containment and map rendering at the crossing remain in review.

The official Zagoria 89 BMP2 releases 1.0.23 and 1.0.25 register `{1EF865DC4E3F7E0B}IFV/BMP2/BMP2_Olive_test.et`. The downloaded WZ Tanks 1.0.120 archive registers a different Olive prefab. The installed Zagoria 1.0.43 replacement uses a different GUID and changes the vehicle class, hatch configuration and other serialized data. Compare behavior before using it as a replacement. The two historical archives were retrieved through the dedicated server in isolated profiles. [Zagoria release history](https://reforger.armaplatform.com/workshop/6730D59067916E3D/changelog) · [WZ Tanks Workshop](https://reforger.armaplatform.com/workshop/61A2FDEE636A1CD8)

An isolated dedicated server downloaded Chungus Shotguns 1.0.43 and compiled its game scripts on Reforger 1.9.0.37. The archived database registers RoleReversal's original 610 mm double barrel and Gigantomachia's Remington 870. The installed 1.0.48 reuses the double barrel's GUID for a 20-inch Coach Gun. With 1.0.43 mounted, the 277-launcher audit proposed both drafts and the installer dry run passed all 37 new files. The standard installed graph rejected the two original weapon paths and the original 12-gauge shell prefab. Both missions stay staged for a deployment that pins the verified dependency and runs the representative mission checks. [Chungus Shotguns release history](https://reforger.armaplatform.com/workshop/620E584B1D2C96A4/changelog)

An external clone committed both drafts and passed the pinned-graph file audit at 178 launchers. The capture preflight verified the two worlds' saved references against the retained graph with RHIB excluded. Workbench session `logs_2026-11-21_16-02-02` generated the fixture resource database, and both loopback dedicated runs produced native receipts with their expected scenario and world IDs and the exact 146-addon closure. See `logs_2026-11-21_16-02-35` and `logs_2026-11-21_16-02-50`. Both sessions reached Pregame but reported an incomplete game-mode replication setup. The startup trace found ProntoHub's stock game-mode override referring to an unavailable `Pronto_AnimRadialMenuComponent`. Removing that addon and its dependents left 11 unresolved saved references in RoleReversal and 36 in Gigantomachia. Both runs reported a map recovery exception, and Gigantomachia also reported drone controller and jammer exceptions. They still require dependency repair, native mission snapshots and playable runtime verification before delivery to Dev.

GC Lobby map recovery now reports an unavailable map before reading native markers. The two isolated dedicated runs in `logs_2026-11-21_16-06-09` and `logs_2026-11-21_16-06-24` reached their expected receipts without the previous map capture exception. The Arland lobby example with Base and Lobby in `logs_2026-11-21_16-07-05` still saved a generation-one recovery journal with four factions. Interactive admin actions, the shared replication setup and Gigantomachia's drone behavior still need verification.

ProntoHub 1.0.101 still reports the missing `Pronto_AnimRadialMenuComponent` when loaded independently on an isolated Reforger 1.9.0.37 dedicated server. The same error occurs in the 1.0.99 package used by the retained mission graph. See `logs_2026-11-21_16-07-52` in the isolated ProntoHub profile. [Pronto Hub release history](https://reforger.armaplatform.com/workshop/631A9C6C92283C44/changelog)

An isolated resources audit with Zagoria 1.0.25 cleared Topdown's files and preserved the original 69 playable slots under the advertised capacity of 68. The installer dry run accepted 16 new files and one reviewed update. With the normal installed dependency graph, the same dry run rejected only the missing historical BMP-2 reference. Topdown remains held for the standard release. The other four worlds that use the original GUID also have conversion work.

Supply each downloaded profile's `addons` directory with `--historical-workshop` on the normal audit. Its `historicalAddonAlternatives` report checks each held draft's exact resource IDs and paths and records the historical addon version, the registry hash and which drafts have every reported blocker covered by that package. The scan uses the active Dev graph for conversion and the supplied archives for discovery.

Repeat the audit using a separate `--workshop-addons` directory with one copy of each addon. Pass the normal audit's `plan.json` with `--compare-provider-plan`. This compares the same legacy and Dev revisions and lists gained and lost file clearance across committed launchers and all ready drafts, including drafts beyond the suggested batch limit. Run the installer against the same selected provider directory to verify the staged files. Check script compilation and runtime in that isolated graph before delivery.

The 195-launcher audit found exact historical registrations for RoleReversal and Gigantomachia in Chungus Shotguns 1.0.43, for Topdown in Zagoria 1.0.25, and for both missing buildings in The Blood and Smoke in ArmaTerrainCore 1.1.7. The isolated 1.1.7 audit cleared The Blood and Smoke and verified all 38 files in fixture commit `02132ddb`. That graph left five confirmed Dev missions with missing scenery references. It also hit `Wirecutter_UserAction.c` using the unavailable `SCR_SoundManagerEntity` on the current engine. ArmaTerrainCore 1.1.8 and 1.1.9 started isolated dedicated servers and both lack the original building registrations. The Blood and Smoke still needs both buildings in a package that compiles on the current engine. [ArmaTerrainCore release history](https://reforger.armaplatform.com/workshop/60B524F7A5AE96A8/changelog)

Two Bloody Miles now retains the Building_01 composition and all 12 placed group overrides. The converter preserves the original resource and entity IDs, updates the stale prefab registration path, and replaces three inherited navmesh components with the equivalent Lobby components. The original local trigger has no flag reader, script consumer, or status messages. The converter retains its named anchor and instance transforms. The three-file composition passed the installed dependency audit. Live group orders, slot transforms and navmesh rebuilds still need comparison.

The crew and spawn converters accept the exact historical BMP-2 registration when the supplied provider database contains it. The isolated audit also identified the authored 150 m mortar-smoke effect from 2nd Break The Line. The converter copies that mission-owned prefab after checking its source digest and retains its native smoke-line parent. With Zagoria 1.0.25, Two Bloody Miles passed the file audit with 26 playable slots and 22 placed spawners. The combined Topdown and Two Bloody Miles installer dry run accepted 38 new files and one reviewed update with that provider. The normal dependency graph rejected only the missing BMP-2 reference. These drafts remain staged outside Missions Dev. The full standard audit kept all 254 previous draft files byte-identical.

The provider comparison repeated the Zagoria 1.0.25 audit against the same 195-launcher Dev revision. The isolated graph cleared the files for Topdown and Two Bloody Miles and retained file clearance for all 195 committed missions. External fixture commit `fb1f851b` records both native Workbench snapshots and pins the test provider to 1.0.25. Workbench captured 224 entities for Topdown and 410 for Two Bloody Miles. Both dedicated starts returned the expected scenario receipt with 146 addons. The server reported powertrain setup errors for all four placed BMP-2s, and both runs also reported an unknown Pronto animation component.

An isolated drivetrain test on the current engine gave the original BMP-2 a native engine-start request under versions 1.0.23 and 1.0.25. In both runs it reported the engine off, zero RPM and zero wheels. The stock truck in the same fixture reported the engine on, 600 RPM and six wheels. Both missions remain outside Missions Dev. The follow-up needs a compatible vehicle that preserves the authored crew stations, equipment and movement. The converter continues to require the original resource unless a replacement passes that comparison.

Lehto Tussle and Bootnecks and BTRs explicitly enable the old shooting restriction during their 300-second staging countdown. The published Lobby handlers `PS_PlayableControllerComponent.c` and `PS_M_SCR_HitZone.c` suppress player attack inputs with an admin/server exception and suppress hit-zone damage independently. Keep these missions held while the replacement only supports a countdown. Bootnecks and BTRs also has two mission-owned slot prefabs to review.

Startup entity cleanup remains a separate behavior gap across worlds with `PK_EntityDeleter`. The published TilW placement includes roots intersecting the volume, optional visible-only or prefab filtering and protection exclusions. The GC radius action uses entity origins, supports building interior expansion and protects its own anchor and game mode. Scouts Out is an unfiltered startup cleanup. Its exact removal set needs evidence before reuse of the current action.

When a legacy placement authors trench progress settings, the converter restores the published Lobby building manager settings and uses an opt-in construction outline registry. It scales the native build threshold for new layouts using the authored preparation duration and multipliers. Missing authored values use the published GC Core defaults of 300 seconds, 2 during preparation and 10 afterwards. The legacy mode and its threshold override were inspected in `GCC_PS_GameModeCoop_M.c` and `GCC_SCR_CampaignBuildingLayoutComponent_M.c`. GC Lobby uses the native outline registry interface. Workbench MCP compiled the subclass with zero errors in session `logs_2026-11-20_20-15-48`. Live inspection of Villeneuf found a second building manager from the inherited ACE Trenches base-mode overlay. The converter now uses the inherited manager and outline slot IDs. The corrected local Villeneuf layer loaded with one building manager in Workbench MCP session `logs_2026-11-20_20-33-16`. Placement, threshold changes and the implied defaults on missions without authored overrides still need review.

The group rule preserves the Role Reversal HVT slot. The published legacy damage component only checks its owner, and the verified CIV group ancestry has no damage manager. Both variants have an independent CIV casualty producer for `HVT_DEAD`. The converter keeps that producer and honours the legacy forced playability setting. The randomized civilian wrapper and its 11 variants map to the same stock variant order and parents, with playability supplied by the native group. The CDF variant retains the original native storage box and all 23 slots. The original Role Reversal still references the old 610 mm shotgun. The dependency now uses the ID for a 20-inch Coach Gun, so the original variant remains in review.

The batch group converter resolves the archived MSV80 platoon leader, deputy and medic by their exact authored GUID and path. It compares the restored Units Dev prefabs with the archived Units commit and uses the historical platoon leader when the placed path identifies that version. The published legacy Lobby platoon-leader and medic parents declare playable characters. A group with an explicit roster that is entirely playable uses the native playable field even when the legacy group had no force-playable override. Mixed AI and playable rosters stay in review. Green Hill Assault has 63 authored slots across both faction layers and retains the 75-player header. The capacity approval checks the source header and both roster layer hashes. Issued equipment and slot presentation need a representative runtime check.

The area converter reports the exact source field or setting that blocked a trigger. Within a verified placement group, an anonymous unconsumed faction trigger can be omitted when status messages are disabled and the flag appears only in its own declaration and has no mission script reference. The other instances retain their trigger areas and event consumers. Operation Tampa retains its two 450 m checks with an at-most-zero faction share and both five-second cleanup actions. Its five civilian AI groups retain their native randomized roster and waypoint assignments. Live faction share at match entry and cover framing still need representative checks.

Verified map markers and passive map shapes attached to sphere triggers stay attached to the generated native area. Their local transforms, names and styles remain authored at the same relative position. Trigger use and marker name checks still apply, including ambiguous names in visibility actions. The converter reports rotated or scaled parents of attached map shapes and nested gameplay triggers as separate cases. Verify client rendering of a representative attached overlay when a complete mission clears its remaining file checks.

The event flag converter handles Set, Clear and negated literal conditions for flags owned entirely by the converted event rules. It requires a converted Set producer, keeps each instruction delay and limits negated triggers and their deliveries to Match. The published TilW Set and Clear instructions use the same flag store and pass opposite Boolean values to `AdjustMissionFlag`. Flags with external producers or script references stay in review. Check simultaneous Set/Clear ordering with a representative mission when one clears the other file checks.

The batch weather rule preserves base-game weather and starting-time settings. It applies active legacy date settings with their original defaults and uses the existing mode-owned environment component for active fog, rain and wind overrides. It drops legacy values whose switches are off. Geographic coordinates, timezone overrides and simultaneous native and legacy fog or wind overrides remain held for review. The legacy lobby's implicit clock reset at Match start remains a separate behavior gap. These decisions follow the published TilW Mission Framework weather extension and the installed base-game handler, inspected through the Reforger MCP archive tools.

The briefing reader follows static child descriptions inside a standard description placement. The published legacy GC Lobby description registers each page independently with the description manager. The generated GC Lobby preset retains the authored text and audience for every page, including children. Pages under other entity types, prefab-owned pages, and scripts that manage briefing lifetimes require separate review. The batch flags any converted delete instruction that targets a named briefing.

The marker rule translates the legacy hidden-state list to GC Lobby phases. Simple thresholds retain their existing representation. Mixed lists use the marker's explicit hidden phases, which are carried in the replicated marker snapshot and checked alongside faction visibility. Workbench MCP compiled the change with zero errors in session `logs_2026-11-20_19-12-27`. File checks covered all 32 Lobby phase combinations, including both legacy numeric values observed in the catalog. Live client rendering and late-join behavior remain unverified. The source phase check was reviewed in the published PS Core manual marker, and the source state order in the published GC Lobby mode. Legacy cutscene and debriefing screens have no separate phase in this conversion.

The batch marker rule preserves the legacy draw order at rest and on hover. Legacy defaults are zero at rest and 10,000 on hover. When `m_bringToFront` is off, hovering keeps the resting order. The migration checks the authored integer range and carries both settings in the replicated marker snapshot. The published PS Core widget and the TilW Mission Framework widget extension supplied the reference behavior. Workbench MCP compiled the change with zero errors in session `logs_2026-11-20_19-16-13`. Rendered overlap and hover behavior still need a live client check.

The marker converter keeps child icons attached to their parent marker. It preserves each local transform, appearance and audience. The published PS Core marker and GC Lobby marker both read world position and yaw. Nested non-marker entities, including legacy map shapes, still require a conversion rule. Zavarak Farmland preserves seven top-level icons and two child icons and is the first candidate for a representative client check of marker nesting. Its BTR-70 references retain their resource IDs. The wreck path follows the base-game database, and the crewed variant has identical prefab content in the Units source and Dev snapshots.

For existing batch-converted worlds, the planner can stage a draw-order repair when the original conversion reproduces the entire Dev marker layer at the same path. The installer verifies the original layer hash and requires `--replace-reviewed`. Six layers matched and received 28 marker corrections in Missions Dev commit `4ff10132`. The dedicated conversion recipes retain their original output.

The batch mode rule preserves explicitly disabled JIP teleport and the legacy opening delay. Despite its name, `m_denyJIPTime` denied requests before the configured time. The rule uses GC Lobby's Match-relative opening time and retains the legacy 60-second floor. GC Lobby's existing connection eligibility, destination checks and single-offer policy still apply. The mode rule also accepts faction respawn tables containing only zero-ticket entries when the table parses cleanly. Funded tables still require scheduling, destination and replacement behavior review. The published GC Core JIP handler and legacy GC Lobby respawn configuration supplied the reference. Workbench MCP compiled the updated JIP window with zero errors in session `logs_2026-11-20_19-23-11`. Remote request timing and delivery remain unverified.

The group rule retains native movement settings, simple editable-group names, preview images and faction labels, member limits, danger range and empty-player deletion settings. It discards the standard legacy callsign assigner on verified AI-only groups. The published legacy GC Lobby uses that component only while registering a playable slot. The base-game Group prefab supplied the native movement and editable-group component identities. Custom UI variants, per-slot color and icon overrides and legacy role prefabs still require review. The batch run reduced group blockers from 359 to 338 and generated four additional standalone roster layers for review. The existing complete drafts remained byte-identical.

The batch reviewer and installer resolve resource references against the Dev addon's declared dependency graph. ## Coverage

The comparison indexes mission headers, including Scenario Framework subclasses, and every committed world. It follows source-local resource GUID references and each subscene's layer tree. The per-world record includes the source header, counts of serialized declarations, authored respawn and freeze overrides, source locations for briefing gaps, and path-level differences against the specified Dev commit. Declaration counts include grouped placement headers and inherited local resources. They are not runtime entity counts. Binary assets and external provider overrides, globally registered Enforce scripts and dynamically resolved names need separate inspection.

The first pass translates placed PS mission descriptions into mission-specific GC Lobby mode prefabs. Each preset inherits the GC Lobby template and holds the scenario's briefing definitions. The selected worlds still require actual mode placement and conversion of their other systems. A world with an unsupported description receives no preset. This prevents a partially parsed group or a missing audience restriction from being published as a complete briefing. Entries with duplicate or out-of-range display indices receive consecutive indices in stable source order after sorting by legacy order. This preserves relative ordering, but external references to legacy indices require review.

The Blood and Smoke uses the expanded notes newly added by legacy commit `9a681ab9`. Its parent contains the shorter notes. The converter resolves only the exact conflicted blob. The launcher staging command resolves the shared Topdown and San Serriffe Busters world identity.

## Preparing launcher resources for assembly

```powershell
python external/development/mission-conversion/launchers.py --missions ../gc-reforger-missions --source origin/master --dev origin/dev --stage "$env:TEMP/gc-launchers" Missions/Delfer/Topdown/Topdown.conf
```

Supply the source header paths for the batch, or omit them to prepare the whole catalog. Each output contains the launcher header, its metadata, and the metadata for the world it loads. Keep these files in staging until the converted world and its layers are ready. The comparison records the resulting reference in `destinationWorld`.

Five headers have outdated paths and Operation Steel has a case difference. Topdown and San Serriffe Busters share the legacy GUID and both source metadata files name SerrifBusters. Busters keeps `321510A1C6838890` and Topdown receives `052737705D787FC7`. Loose Ends regains its historical launcher identity `2B73EAFD3FFE9D0B` from the metadata preceding its removal in commit `5489ae66`. Checks on the staged catalog resolved all 277 headers and found 554 distinct header and world identities. Map previews, external references and in-engine registration need verification with the assembled missions.

| Source behavior | GC Lobby comparison and pending work |
| --- | --- |
| Phase and mode ownership | Replace the legacy root once per world, preserving terrain AI, perception, faction overrides, weather, chat and radio ownership. Check lobby/roles → briefing → match → after-action report on authority and clients. |
| Groups and roles | Resolve Units Dev parents by GUID. Compare each placed group's playable members, descriptions, assigned callsign indices, custom units and original positions. A standalone playable character requires an explicit slot solution. |
| Icon markers and map shapes | Resolve inherited icon, highlight, quad, rotation, color, world size, label and phase/audience. Check visibility before slotting and as each side. Legacy outline widths are measured in metres while GC passive shape widths are in pixels. |
| Briefing audience | Preserve unassigned, listed and all assigned audiences independently. Record unsupported layouts and nested ownership per world. Verify ordering, content and audience on the live UI. |
| Tickets and respawn | Audit finite faction budgets, per-death delays, waves, per-character replacement lists and named destinations separately. Legacy PS schedules its serialized interval directly on the call queue. Do not infer units from the editor label or translate per-death timers into waves. |
| Framework events | Trace every flag producer, expression, action, delay and reactivation. Legacy per-instruction delays default to five seconds. GC event delays recheck conditions. Legacy player casualty flags use historical maximum concurrent living players and can clear; GC casualty conditions count deaths of the starting roster. |
| Victory and AAR | The legacy Core framework overlay sets `m_suppressGameEnd 1`. Resolve per-instance changes before translating a notification into an actual match ending. GC end actions start an adjustable countdown. |
| Special scenarios | Roulette and Commandos have mission-specific scripts and shared player-controller hooks on master. Port their actual behavior and isolate it to the intended mode before loading those scripts on Dev. Review the native Advance and Secure / Advance and Cooperate worlds independently. |

Sources for the legacy contracts include Reforger Lobby Community's `PS_MissionDescription`, `PS_MissionDescriptionHeadersListUI` and `PS_GameModeCoop`, and TilW Mission Framework's `TILW_Instructions.c`, `TILW_MissionFrameworkEntity.c` and `TILW_MapShapeComponent.c`. GC Lobby contracts are in `scripts/Game/Briefing`, `scripts/Game/Map` and `scripts/Game/MissionFramework`. The converter has no runtime dependency on the old framework.

Review each launcher, world, roster and behavior against the legacy files before delivery. Record unsupported behavior by mission and use representative live checks for new shared runtime behavior.

Keep mission commits local while preparing and verifying the batch. Push substantial batches of roughly ten converted missions together with their required GC Lobby and Units changes. Count mission worlds in the batch and record the remaining behavior gaps for each one.

Add `--include-race-day` to stage the Race Day – Kunar launcher header, world, and layers alongside its settings preset. The recipe checks the legacy rules blob before rewriting its events. The port uses the race motorbike from Units Dev commit `358ce612`. The playable world files are in Missions Dev commit `2a334cc5`.

Add `--stage-marker-candidates` for standalone icon layers. Inspect the `markerLayers` record per world. Each entry gives an icon count or the first unsupported placement, inherited prefab, or field. At the pinned source revision 53 layers containing 403 icons can be staged. These require resource, phase, faction, stacking, hover and visual checks on their owning world before publication. Other map shapes, nested markers and script-created markers require separate conversion.
